title: Sort and limit the result
summary: ORDER BY chooses the result order. LIMIT then keeps only the requested number of rows.
introduction: ORDER BY chooses the result order. LIMIT then keeps only the requested number of rows. Your task: Return the two longest books.
learningObjectives: Explain the example for sort and limit the result

blocks.text: ORDER BY chooses the result order. LIMIT then keeps only the requested number of rows.
Use the SQL Run button for examples marked runnable. They use this site's in-browser SQLite database and sample-only table names. A Python example needs Python on your own computer instead.

blocks.code:
WITH books(title,pages) AS (VALUES('Moon Trip',60),('Tiny Seed',20),('Garden Days',40))
SELECT title FROM books ORDER BY pages,title LIMIT 2;
blocks.title: Sort and limit the result

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `ORDER BY` chooses a result order. Include a tie-break field when equal values need a stable order.
`SELECT` names the output values. `AS` can give a calculated result a readable column name.

blocks.text: Tiny Seed and Garden Days are returned in that order.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Do not rely on table storage order. Add ORDER BY whenever order matters.
